title: Payどん operator Infcurion hit by unauthorized access; 251,172 records leaked, service suspended
date_note: Date of the joint notice by the four banks and Infcurion; they received Infcurion's report on 19 November.
summary: Four Kagoshima financial institutions said Infcurion, which operates the Payどん payment system for them, reported unauthorized access on 19 November, and that 251,172 records of personal information leaked. All Payどん services were stopped at 6:20 on 20 November. They say they applied an urgent patch and blocked the intrusion route; the cause is under investigation. INTERNET Watch reports Tsuruha Group's HAPPAY, which also uses Infcurion's Wallet Station platform, suspended service as a precaution.
plain: The Payどん payment app run for four Kagoshima financial institutions was breached through its operator; 251,172 records leaked and the service is stopped. Another service on the same platform, HAPPAY, also paused.
exec: A payment-service vendor breach exposed 251,172 records and forced a full service stop at four regional lenders.
action: Payどん users: do not enter PINs or passwords at links in messages; Infcurion warns of phishing calls, emails and SMS and says no misuse is confirmed.
geo_basis: the four banks running Payどん are in Kagoshima Prefecture; Infcurion's own location not stated on the pages read

sources.name: Kagoshima Bank (joint notice of four institutions)

validation.note: Primary notices by the four institutions and by Infcurion, plus Cybersecurity.com. Infcurion's page gives no record count; the figure is from the banks' notice.

review.note: Compared with Kagin joint notice, Infcurion and Cybersecurity.com: 251,172, 19/20 Nov, 6:20 stop, patch statement match; two of the four institutions are shinkin banks, wording changed to financial institutions
